criteria.criterion: defaults.toml has a new [[default]] entry (e.g. id "behavior-evidence") with applies_to ["*"], a source citing this request, and a statement whose FIRST sentence says criteria must check the requested behavior happening, not that types, files or wiring exist.
criteria.evidence: Read in the diff: the new [[default]] has id "behavior-evidence", applies_to = ["*"], and source "job 20261015-141831-hyb4 (retry of 20261015-095214-y8kr)...". Its first sentence is "Acceptance criteria must check the requested behavior happening, not that types, files or wiring exist."

criteria.criterion: The statement's later sentences require that a protection or denial test first shows the action succeeds without the protection, as the same user and environment the real component runs as (root), then shows it is refused, and that it fails, not skips or passes silently, if the environment cannot enforce the protection.
criteria.evidence: Read in the diff: the second sentence says the test "first shows the action succeeds without the protection, as the same user and in the same environment the real component runs as (root), then shows the action is refused". The third says "It fails, not skips or passes silently, if the environment cannot enforce the protection; a file mode that root bypasses is not proof."

criteria.criterion: A new unit test in crates/athena-data/src/defaults.rs parses the repository defaults.toml and asserts the new entry exists and its render() line contains the core rule. Run `cargo test -p athena-data`: it passes along with root_cause_default_leads_with_the_core_rule.
criteria.evidence: The new test behavior_evidence_default_leads_with_the_core_rule parses REPO_DEFAULTS, gets "behavior-evidence", checks that applies_to is ["*"], and asserts that render() contains the full first-sentence line. It would fail without the entry. I ran `cargo test -p athena-data`: 64 passed, including both behavior_evidence_default_leads_with_the_core_rule and root_cause_default_leads_with_the_core_rule.

criteria.criterion: docs/design/defaults-loop.md has a worked example for a 'make X read-only' request whose criteria are: a write to X as root succeeds before protection; the same root write is refused after; the test fails, not skips, if the environment cannot enforce it (a root-bypassed file mode is not proof).
criteria.evidence: New §3.7, under "Make X read-only.", lists three criteria: (1) a root write succeeds before the protection; (2) the same root write is refused after it; (3) the test fails, not skips or passes silently, if the environment cannot enforce the protection, and "A file mode that root bypasses is not proof".

criteria.criterion: The same doc has a worked example for 'role calls a model' whose criteria run the role end to end and check the model request is observed (e.g. through the fake client) and its output is used, not merely that a client or config is wired in.
criteria.evidence: §3.7, under "The review role calls a model.": run the role end to end with the fake client; assert the fake client observed the request and check what it received; assert the role's output contains or derives from the fake reply. It contrasts these with wiring checks ("a client type exists", "the config names a model").

criteria.criterion: Outcome check for the reader: the rendered reader brief for the defaults set includes the new default line with the core rule, so a reader writing criteria for a read-only request sees it. Check by running the athena-context tests, which must still pass within the reader token budget.
criteria.evidence: The reader set in crates/athena-cli/tests/budgets.rs is built from the contract, READER_FRAME, defaults.render() and the catalog. The new defaults.rs test asserts that render() contains the behavior-evidence line, so the reader receives it. `cargo test -p athena-context`: 31 passed. `cargo test -p athena-cli --test budgets -- --nocapture` printed "reader 1969", within the new budget of 2,000. That also confirms the old 1,930 budget would have been exceeded.

criteria.criterion: `git diff` shows no collateral edits: crates/athena-context/prompts/reader.md is unchanged, or, if changed, differs only by the intended lines with every instruction still its own bullet. Each CHANGELOG.md claim under Unreleased / Added names only things present in the diff, with no claim about the reader prompt unless reader.md contains it.
criteria.evidence: `git diff HEAD~1 --stat` lists six files and reader.md is not among them. Every CHANGELOG claim checks out: the defaults entry is present; the unit test is in defaults.rs; §3.7 has two examples; the reader set went over 1,930 (measured 1969); the budget in lib.rs is now 2_000; D25 in docs/decisions.md records it (the heading at line 608 is D25); and the reader prompt is unchanged.

criteria.criterion: `cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` all pass from the repository root.
criteria.evidence: `cargo fmt --check` passed; it was the first part of a chained command whose second part I mistyped with an invalid `-q` passed to clippy-driver. I then ran `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` cleanly, and `cargo test --quiet` reported every suite ok with 0 failures.

findings.summary: Unclear wording in the read-only example: "the first write" should say "the root write".
findings.evidence: Step 3 says "if the first write still succeeds after the mode change, the test fails". "First write" refers to step 1's write, which happens before the protection. "The root write" would be clearer.

findings.summary: The reader budget was raised rather than paid for with removals.
findings.evidence: check_budget's message says "pay for additions with removals". The change raises BudgetSet::Reader from 1,930 to 2,000 instead, recorded in D25 and the CHANGELOG. The measured reader set of 1969 tokens shows the raise was needed, and the reading allows a budget-forced change. Still, the same thing could happen again; raising the budget is a choice the changelog states openly.

summary: The change passes. It does what the retry asked: a new `behavior-evidence` default in defaults.toml, applying to every role, whose first sentence states the core rule. Its later sentences require a protection test to show the action succeeding as root without the protection, then refused, and to fail rather than skip if the environment cannot enforce it. A unit test in defaults.rs pins the rendered line. defaults-loop.md §3.7 adds the two worked examples. Adding the line pushed the reader set to 1969 tokens, over the old 1,930 budget (measured), so the budget is now 2,000 and D25 records why. reader.md is untouched, and every CHANGELOG claim matches the diff. All changed files are on the deliverables list. I ran `cargo test -p athena-data`, `cargo test -p athena-context`, the reader budget test, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test`; all passed. One minor point: the budget was raised instead of paid for with removals. One nit: a wording slip in the read-only example.
